newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australia 10-yr bond sags,clings to 92.250.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australia 10-yr bond sags,clings to 92.250.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract was clinging to support at 92.250 at the end of SYCOM trade, some 12 basis points below Tuesday's 11-week high.
*Contract sags amid disappointment over the 1997/98 budget statement and weak U.S. Treasuries.
The Australian 10-year bond futures contract was clinging to support at 92.250 at the end of SYCOM trade, some 12 basis points below Tuesday's 11-week high.
The contract ended Tuesday's special evening pit session for the 1997/98 budget at 92.280 after finishing the usual dayside session at 92.345 and down from a high of 92.370.
The rapid reversal from new highs will weigh on the market with a slide to support at 92.180 seen as likely, and analysts said further moves to 92.080/92.100 can not be ruled.
Disappointment over the 1997/98 budget statement was fuelled by a weak U.S. Treasury market.

Treasurer Peter Costello predicted a larger-than-expected underlying budget deficit of A$3.9 billion and a headline budget surplus of A$6.4 billion, well short of the A$10 billion mark that had been speculated in the run-up to the budget.
The underlying deficit for 1996/97 is projected at A$6.9 billion.

"The Budget was a step in the right direction. While it may not have stepped as far as financial markets would have liked, it achieved its aims with relatively little pain," said chief economist Hans Kunnen in Colonial State Bank's budget summary.
Moody's Investors Service said that the Australian budget would have no impact on the nation's Aa2 sovereign debt rating and said the outlook was stable.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries weakened as the market refocused on next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting where a decision on interest rates is still far from clear.
The market had firmed initially after retail sales data for April fell 0.3 percent.
